title: Context Engineering for AI Agents | Clara by Faros

hero.headline: Context in. Rework out.
hero.subhead: Bootstrap your AI coding agents with institutional knowledge. Less WTF code. More one-shot success.

sections.heading: How we help
sections.body: AI that unlocks productivity instead of shifting bottlenecks: automate context delivery, accelerate agentic PRs, maintain human oversight.

sections.heading: Historical replay — give your agents tenure, overnight
sections.body: Feeds agents context derived from past PRs and tickets until success rates soar; per-repo context generation including patterns, dependencies, and failure modes; rules battle-tested in replay simulations.

sections.heading: Agentic PR delivery — assign Faros, get a PR
sections.body: Context planted into agentic workflows for ready-to-merge code: automatic Jira ticket enhancement, disambiguated implementation plans that flag open issues, code generation with Claude, Codex, Copilot, Cursor.

sections.heading: Human oversight — humans-in-the-loop, by design
sections.body: Faros generates a PR; developers review and merge. Developer feedback becomes reusable context so agents don't ask twice; context can train new hires.

sections.heading: Continuous learning — self-optimizing as your codebase evolves
sections.body: Captures feedback from every merged PR and review to refine agent behavior; updates the context graph from completed tasks; generates digests for engineers.

notes: The capability is branded 'Clara' (page title). This is the live, named surface most relevant to the seed tree's Optimize/Govern roadmap items: 'historical replay' is shipped/branded here (offering.json lists Historical Replay as 'partial'); 'feedback becomes reusable context so agents don't ask twice' is the closest public analog to the repo's roadmap 'Negative Memory / Context Write-back' — but the page frames it as forward learning, not explicitly writing failure lessons back. Honesty for any negative-memory mapping should stay 'inference'. Human-in-the-loop framing corroborates the 'empower not police' principle.
